Subject: Light Up a Life 2026 — draft for Moira to review

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the bookshop window again this year. Hilary asked on the page the other day whether we were doing it, as her mum’s name was on it last year. Yes, Hilary, we are, and we shall be very pleased to see you and your sister.

It is seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on the tree, I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the shop counter, with the same pen. I still have to take a moment, but it has become one of the things I want to do each November.

I know there will be people writing a name for the first time this year, and others who have been bringing the same name for much longer than I have. There is room for all of us. You don’t have to have had someone cared for by the hospice to put a name on the tree. It is for anyone who is grieving, whether the person you miss died recently or many years ago.

Memory tags will be available in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take yours home to write. Some things are easier at your own kitchen table, and there is no need to find the words while somebody is waiting behind you.

We shall switch on the lights on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is making mince pies again. Those who came last year will remember that you had to be fairly quick for a mince pie.

Every name on the tags will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December, at 3pm in the day centre. You do not have to attend the service for your loved one’s name to be read.

Thank you to everyone who helped make last year’s tree what it was. It carried 412 names, and each one mattered to somebody. Thank you for bringing them, for coming along, and for being kind to one another on a cold evening in Magdalen Street.

And please remember that you can simply come and stand by the tree. You needn’t buy a book, or anything else. You needn’t explain why you have come, either. If a quiet few minutes by the window is what you would like, you are very welcome.

Jean
